metadata.note: Q2ai(1m): name 3 states of matter for water in 3 slots. Q2aii(3m): match each state to its particle energy description (1m each). 6 slots total. Combined into one DDWTOS for cohesion. Q2ai slots 1-3: solid/liquid/gas. Q2aii slots 4-6: particle energy description for solid/liquid/gas respectively. Distractors for states: plasma/vapour. Distractors for energy: opposites.

question.name: CSEC Chem May 2023 Q2a(i)(ii) — States of Matter and Particle Energy
question.text:

question.general_feedback:
States of matter and particle energy:

StateParticle energyArrangement
SolidLowest energy; particles vibrate in fixed positionsClosely packed, regular lattice
LiquidModerate energy; particles can flow past each otherClose together but random
GasHighest energy; particles move rapidly and randomlyFar apart, fill container

Water example: ice (solid) → water (liquid) → steam (gas). Energy increases with each state change (absorbed from surroundings).

groups.label: State with definite shape and definite volume
groups.diagnostic_hint: A SOLID has a definite shape and definite volume. Particles are arranged in a regular lattice and vibrate in fixed positions — they cannot flow or be compressed.

groups.label: State with no definite shape but definite volume
groups.diagnostic_hint: A LIQUID has no definite shape (it takes the shape of its container) but has a definite volume. Particles are close together but free to move/slide past each other.

groups.label: State with no definite shape and no definite volume
groups.diagnostic_hint: A GAS has no definite shape and no definite volume. Particles are far apart, moving rapidly and randomly, and can be compressed.

options.text: Particles have the lowest energy; they vibrate in fixed positions
Particles have moderate energy; they can flow and slide past each other
Particles have the highest energy; they move rapidly and randomly

groups.label: Particle energy description — Solid
groups.diagnostic_hint: Solid particles have the LOWEST energy — they only vibrate about fixed positions in a regular lattice. They cannot move past each other.

options.text: Particles have the lowest energy; they vibrate in fixed positions
Particles have moderate energy; they can flow and slide past each other
Particles have the highest energy; they move rapidly and randomly

groups.label: Particle energy description — Liquid
groups.diagnostic_hint: Liquid particles have MODERATE energy — enough to move and flow past each other, but not enough to overcome intermolecular forces and escape into the gas phase.

options.text: Particles have the lowest energy; they vibrate in fixed positions
Particles have moderate energy; they can flow and slide past each other
Particles have the highest energy; they move rapidly and randomly

groups.label: Particle energy description — Gas
groups.diagnostic_hint: Gas particles have the HIGHEST energy — they move rapidly and randomly, with large distances between them. They can fill any container and be compressed.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 8 tokens for 6 slots. States word bank (slots 1-3): 'Plasma' is the fourth state of matter but not relevant to water at normal conditions; 'Vapour' is sometimes used colloquially for steam but is not the correct scientific term for the gaseous state in this context (gas is the state, vapour implies near-liquid conditions). Energy descriptions (slots 4-6): each description is uniquely matched to its state — students must know the energy ordering: solid (lowest) < liquid (moderate) < gas (highest). The descriptions include both the energy level and the particle motion, requiring understanding rather than recall.
